p: Planning a birthday here? Climbing parties work best when everyone arrives together, because the harness fitting and safety talk happen as a group and latecomers can end up missing precious wall time. Send the invitations with a reminder about trainers and comfy clothes, and ask parents to leave rings and bracelets at home. Spectating grown-ups get a great view from the floor, so have phones ready for that triumphant moment someone slaps the top of the wall for the first time.

Walton-on-Thames is surrounded by brilliant days out. Hampton Court Palace, Henry VIII's grand riverside palace, is just a short drive or river walk away, with its famous maze and magnificent gardens. Brooklands Museum in Weybridge sits on the site of the world's first purpose-built motor racing circuit and has historic cars, aircraft and a Concorde you can step aboard.

Thrill-seekers might want to head to Thorpe Park near Chertsey, packed with big rollercoasters and water rides. For a gentler pace, Painshill in Cobham is an 18th-century landscape garden with a crystal grotto, follies and a lake, while Claremont Landscape Garden near Esher has a lake and amphitheatre to explore. The Thames Path through Walton is lovely for a stroll, and Walton Bridge makes a good viewpoint. Walton station has regular trains to London Waterloo, making it easy to reach without a car.
